pr.title: [Merged by Bors] - chore(Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic): remove redundant `fun_` lemmas
pr.body:
This PR removes some lemmas `fun_deriv` and `fun_iterated_deriv`, because they are purely eta-expanded forms of existing lemmas. There is no scenario where these lemmas would be more useful than the existing lemmas.

Since the lemmas are very new, they don't need a deprecation.

issue_comments.body: @kebekus I believe you added them; what do you think about this PR? What was your original motivation to add the eta-expanded forms?
This PR itself it straightforward; the main question is whether we want it.
He did remove these forms of lemmas after I suggested this on the more recent PR #33117

@grunweg Thanks for asking. I added `fun_deriv` and `fun_iterated_deriv` because I kept running into missing `fun_` versions. So, I whenever I wrote a new theorem, I added a `fun_` version. When Jovan pointed out that the `fun_` versions of  `deriv`  and `iterated_deriv` are pointless, I experimented a little and came to the conclusion that he is probably right -- within a huge margin of error because of my limited understanding of the technical metaprogramming details. So, I removed the theorem as Jovan suggested … and did not run into problems anywhere.

@kebekus Thanks for the explanation! Let's only add `fun_` versions as needed then --- as these lemmas are unused, let's remove them.
